feedback.quote: A sense of life is a pre-conceptual equivalent of metaphysics, an emotional, subconsciously integrated appraisal of man and of existence.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "The Psycho-Epistemology of Art," The Romantic Manifesto, 24
feedback.note: The passage makes the appraisal pre-conceptual, emotional, and subconsciously integrated, and it names both man and existence. An explicit proof would be conceptual and evidentiary, which this is not. Feeling as a tool of cognition contradicts the status of an appraisal. A one-event mood drops both objects. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Which remark reduces a sense of life to an explicit philosophy under another name?

choices.text: It is simply the system you could already write out, with the same proofs
It appraises before it has been translated into explicit ideas
It is emotional and subconsciously integrated
It concerns both what one takes man to be and what one takes existence to be

feedback.note: Calling it a system already written out, with proofs, erases the pre-conceptual status. The appraisal is in place before that translation, it is emotional and subconsciously integrated, and it appraises both man and existence. Those are the features the reduction drops. Translation can come later; it is not the sense of life itself. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A sense of life is a pre-conceptual emotional appraisal of man and of existence. A finished proof and a tool that discovers facts are the two errors: one turns it into explicit philosophy, the other treats feeling as cognition. Either change drops the definition, because the appraisal is not evidence and not a stated system.

exercises.prompt: When a sense of life has man as its object, what does it appraise?

choices.text: What kind of being one takes a human being to be
Which job a particular stranger should accept
A measurement of one body, offered as a metaphysics
A command that others must live for the group

feedback.note: The appraisal of man answers what one takes a human being to be, as a kind of being. A job for one stranger is a particular decision, not that appraisal. A body measurement is not a view of man's nature. A command to live for the group is an ethical or political demand, and it does not name the object of the sense of life.

exercises.prompt: Someone meets a hard problem and immediately feels, "A person can think this through." What is being appraised?

choices.text: Man, as a being able to face difficulty by the use of his mind
The objects in the room, listed as existence
The fact that this problem is solvable, discovered by the feeling
An explicit philosophy already set out in propositions

feedback.note: The feeling appraises man as able to think through difficulty. It does not inventory the room, which would be a different object, and it does not discover that this problem is in fact solvable. That last step treats the feeling as a tool of cognition. Nor is the feeling already an explicit philosophy; it is the pre-conceptual appraisal.

exercises.prompt: Which item is an appraisal of man held as a sense of life, rather than as an explicit argument?

choices.text: A settled emotional conviction that a human being is a chooser, held before it is argued
A syllogism that derives volition from prior premises
A set of citations assembled to answer a critic
A definition read aloud from a glossary

feedback.note: The emotional conviction, held before argument, is the sense-of-life appraisal of man as a chooser. A syllogism, a set of citations, and a glossary definition are explicit, conceptual performances. They may later translate the appraisal, but they are not the appraisal. Treating them as the sense of life skips its pre-conceptual form. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Match each emotional conviction to the view of man it appraises.

pairs.right: Man appraised as a volitional being

pairs.left: A person is a puppet of forces
pairs.right: Man appraised as determined

pairs.left: A person can achieve his values
pairs.right: Man appraised as efficacious

feedback.note: Each line is an appraisal of what one takes a human being to be: chooser, puppet, or efficacious agent. They are not yet proofs, and a gloomy one does not discover that man is helpless. Efficacy here is still about man. Existence as the world he faces is the other object, and it is not what these three lines name.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of what an appraisal of man takes as its object.

to be, and the feeling is not a

feedback.note: The object is a human being: what kind of being one takes man to be. Proof is the error of treating the feeling as evidence. A sale price and a grammar tip are not appraisals of man at all. The feeling can later be translated into ideas, but that translation does not make the original appraisal a discovery of facts.

exercises.prompt: Someone's sense of life appraises man as a helpless fragment. What does that appraisal do?

choices.text: It emotionally states what he takes a human being to be, and it does not prove the helplessness
It discovers, by its gloom, that man is in fact helpless
It is already an explicit treatise on determinism
It appraises only existence, and says nothing about man

feedback.note: The bleak feeling is still an appraisal of man, and a false or grim appraisal does not prove itself. Gloom used as discovery treats emotion as a tool of cognition. An unstated feeling is not yet a treatise. And the object here is man, not existence alone. The appraisal can be translated later and then checked.

exercises.prompt: Two people witness the same rescue. One feels that a human being can rise to it; the other feels that people are puppets. What differs?

choices.text: What each takes a human being to be, not the fact the feeling is supposed to have proved
The number of people in the street, which the feeling counts
Nothing, because the stronger feeling is automatically true
Their grammar, because an appraisal of man is a usage rule

feedback.note: The scene is shared; the difference is the appraisal of man. Neither feeling proves what a human being is. Intensity as truth is subjectivism. A head count is not this appraisal, and grammar is not a metaphysical estimate of man. The two senses of life contradict each other and still explain nothing by their heat. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim about the appraisal of man in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A sense of life appraises what one takes a human being to be. Proving a fact by the intensity of a feeling would turn the appraisal into a tool of cognition, which it is not. The substitutes change the claim because an emotional estimate of man's nature is not evidence, however settled or strong it feels.

exercises.prompt: When a sense of life has existence as its object, what does it appraise?

choices.text: What one takes the world a human being faces to be
Only what one takes a human being's faculty of choice to be
A catalog of every object in one room
A price put on the world by a market

feedback.note: The appraisal of existence estimates the world a human being faces, for example whether it is knowable and whether achievement is possible in it. The faculty of choice is the appraisal of man, a different object. A room catalog is a list of particulars, not that estimate. A market price is not a view of existence. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Which question belongs to the appraisal of existence?

choices.text: Is the universe knowable, and is achievement possible in it?
Is this person a chooser or a puppet?
What did this witness say at Tuesday's hearing?
Which policy should win the next vote?

feedback.note: Knowability and the possibility of achievement appraise existence. Chooser or puppet appraises man. A witness statement is a particular fact, not a sense of life, and a vote is a political choice. Using the feeling to settle the witness or the vote would also treat it as a tool that discovers facts. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: A person faces a hard task and feels, "The world defeats effort no matter what one knows." What is that feeling?

choices.text: An emotional appraisal of existence as closed to human achievement
A proof that the task is impossible
An appraisal of the grammar in the instructions
An explicit metaphysical essay

feedback.note: The feeling appraises existence as closed to achievement. It does not prove the task impossible; that would make the emotion a tool of cognition. Grammar is not the object, and an unstated feeling is not yet an essay. The appraisal can be translated into the idea of a world in which effort is futile, and then examined.

exercises.prompt: Match each appraisal to the view of existence it expresses.

pairs.right: Existence open to the mind
Existence closed to understanding
Existence open to achievement

feedback.note: These are appraisals of existence, not of man's faculty of choice and not proofs. Open to the mind, closed to understanding, and open to achievement are three estimates of the world a person faces. A bright feeling does not make the benevolent estimate true, and a grim one does not discover that effort is futile.

feedback.note: The world is the object: what one takes existence to be. A proof would discover a fact, which a feeling does not do. A price and a vote are the market and political substitutes, and neither is an emotional estimate of existence. The appraisal remains pre-conceptual even when its object is the whole world one faces.

exercises.prompt: Which remark uses an appraisal of existence as if it discovered a fact?

choices.text: I feel the world is unknowable, so inquiry is pointless and the feeling has settled it

exercises.prompt: Why is pleasure on a holiday not yet an appraisal of existence?

Any pleasure is already a metaphysics of a benevolent universe
Existence can be appraised only after a book is published

The object is the world, held as an emotional estimate. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

feedback.note: An appraisal of existence estimates what one takes the world to be. Proving the facts by a passing mood would make a feeling both a tool of cognition and a one-occasion reaction, which a sense of life is not. The substitutes change the claim because the estimate is pre-conceptual and concerns existence, not a demonstration and not a holiday.

exercises.prompt: When is a sense of life in place, relative to an explicit philosophy?

choices.text: Before it is translated into explicit ideas
Only after a system has been written and memorized
Only while a proof is being recited

feedback.note: The appraisal is pre-conceptual: it is emotionally in place before anyone states it as philosophy. A memorized system and a recited proof come after, if they come at all. Denying that a feeling can precede the statement erases the subconscious integration. The order is appraisal first, translation later. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: What can happen later to a sense of life?

choices.text: It can be translated into explicit ideas, and then examined
It becomes infallible once it is intense
It discovers facts it never had to check
It must be discarded, because translation is impossible

feedback.note: Translation puts the appraisal into ideas so that one can examine it. Intensity does not make it infallible, and the feeling still does not discover facts. Those two errors treat it as a proof. Translation is possible; discarding the appraisal because words can follow it confuses the original estimate with the later statement.

exercises.prompt: A student says, "If the feeling is in place before philosophy, then it is already evidence." What is the error?

choices.text: Confusing a pre-conceptual appraisal with a proof
Noticing that the appraisal precedes the explicit statement
Allowing the appraisal to be translated into ideas
Naming both man and existence as its objects

feedback.note: Priority in time does not confer evidentiary status. The feeling is in place first, and it can be translated, and it does appraise man and existence. None of that makes it evidence. The error is the inference from "before philosophy" to "already a proof," which treats an emotional appraisal as a tool of cognition.

exercises.prompt: Match each stage to the role it has in this account.

pairs.right: The appraisal is already emotionally in place
The appraisal put into explicit ideas
Intensity does not turn the feeling into evidence

feedback.note: The three lines keep an order and a limit. The sense of life precedes explicit philosophy, translation states it, and intensity still is not evidence. Dropping the limit would make the early feeling a mystic revelation or a proof. Dropping the order would make the appraisal impossible until a system is written. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Why does translating the feeling into ideas not make the original feeling a tool of cognition?

Once translated, the feeling retroactively becomes the evidence

exercises.prompt: Which omission breaks the whole account?

Holding the appraisal below the level of a stated philosophy

exercises.prompt: Which rival treats a sense of life as mysticism?

choices.text: It is an ineffable revelation, beyond any later statement in ideas
It can be translated into ideas and then checked
It appraises man and existence together
It is not a tool that discovers facts

feedback.note: Mysticism here means a revelation beyond reason, closed to later statement. A sense of life can be translated into ideas and checked; it is not ineffable. It does appraise both objects, and it is not a tool of cognition. The mystic reading keeps the emotion and drops the possibility of conceptual translation, which the account requires. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Build the whole definition in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A sense of life integrates an appraisal of man with an appraisal of existence. An explicit proof and a tool of cognition are the two reductions that destroy it. The substitutes change the claim because the appraisal is emotional and pre-conceptual, it can be translated later, and the feeling does not discover the facts it estimates.

exercises.prompt: What kind of consciousness has the need for art?

choices.text: A conceptual consciousness, which acquires knowledge by abstractions
A consciousness that never leaves the immediate perceptual moment
Only a consciousness that has finished every practical task
Only a consciousness that treats feeling as a tool of cognition

feedback.note: The need belongs to a conceptual consciousness because man acquires knowledge by abstractions. A mind that never leaves the immediate moment does not hold those wide abstractions. Finished practical tasks are the luxury error, not the subject of the need. Feeling as a tool of cognition is a different mistake and does not identify who needs art.

exercises.prompt: Why does the immediate perceptual moment not solve this mind's problem?

choices.text: Its widest abstractions are not present as one immediate perception
It has no use for perception of any kind
It knows only by a revelation beyond concepts
It cannot form abstractions, so nothing needs integrating

feedback.note: Abstractions are the form of this mind's widest knowledge, and a single percept does not hold them. The mind still needs perception; the problem is to bring the abstractions into it. Revelation beyond concepts is mysticism. The claim that it forms no abstractions describes a different consciousness, not the one that has the need.

exercises.prompt: Which being is the subject of this need?

choices.text: Man, because he lives by concepts rather than by the immediate moment alone
Any organism whose senses register a color
A mind that acquires nothing by abstraction
A crowd, taken as a consciousness above the individuals in it

feedback.note: Man is the conceptual being, so the need is his. Registering a color is not yet living by abstractions. A mind with no abstractions does not have this problem to solve. A crowd above individuals is not a consciousness that acquires knowledge. The need tracks the kind of awareness, which is individual and conceptual.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the scale it has in this need.

pairs.right: The mind that knows by abstractions
Integrations too large for one percept
The awareness that does not have this need

feedback.note: The conceptual mind knows by abstractions, the widest of which are metaphysical and are not one percept, and the mind of the immediate moment does not face that gap. Art answers the gap by concretizing those abstractions. Calling every sensory creature the subject, or calling art a substitute for concepts, swaps these rows.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast that identifies who has the need.

parts.text: The need belongs to a mind that knows by

feedback.note: Abstractions name the conceptual form of knowledge, and the moment names the perceptual present that is not enough. Visions would make the mind mystical, and orders would make it political. Neither is the reason art is needed. The mind that forms wide abstractions is the one that needs them brought into perceptual awareness. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Which remark is skepticism about the need for art?

choices.text: Abstractions never reach reality, so there is nothing for art to make perceptible
Man knows by abstractions formed from what the senses provide
A conceptual mind can hold a view of existence
Metaphysical abstractions are wider than a single percept

feedback.note: If abstractions never reached reality, there would be no metaphysics to concretize and no need of the kind this account names. That is skepticism about conceptual knowledge. The other lines state the basis of the need: abstractions from the senses, a view of existence, and a width no single percept holds. The skeptical remark denies the content art exists to show.

exercises.prompt: Someone says art is for people who cannot think in concepts, a refuge from abstraction. What is reversed?

choices.text: Art is a need of the mind that does think in concepts, not a refuge from them
Art is a need of a mind that stays inside one percept
Concepts are a spare pleasure added after art is finished
Abstractions are already single perceptions, so no need arises

feedback.note: The need arises because the mind thinks in concepts, not because it fails to. A mind stuck in one percept is the wrong subject. Treating concepts as a spare pleasure reverses the dependence again. And abstractions are not already single perceptions; that denial is why the need arises. Art serves conceptual awareness rather than replacing it.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim about who has the need in the order that keeps its meaning.

tokens.text: of a mind stuck in the moment

feedback.note: Art is a need of a conceptual consciousness that knows by abstractions. A mind stuck in the moment does not have the need, and revelation is mysticism rather than conceptual knowledge. The substitutes change the claim because the need follows from the width of abstractions, which must be brought into immediate perceptual awareness.

exercises.prompt: Which claim about art does this account deny?

choices.text: That art is a luxury one may skip once practical needs are met
That a conceptual consciousness needs it
That it re-creates reality according to metaphysical value-judgments
That man's widest knowledge is held in abstractions

feedback.note: The denied claim is that art is a luxury retired by food, shelter, or spare time. The need of a conceptual consciousness, the definition of art, and the fact that knowledge is abstract are affirmed, not denied. Skipping art after practical comfort treats a need of man's kind of awareness as an optional extra.

exercises.prompt: Someone has food, shelter, and free evenings, and concludes that art is unnecessary. What is the false step?

choices.text: Treating art as a spare pleasure that practical comfort can retire
Noticing that food and shelter are needs of a living organism
Admitting that a free evening can be spent on a work of art
Granting that a conceptual mind acquires knowledge by abstractions

feedback.note: Food and shelter are real needs, and a free evening may be used for art. Neither fact retires the need of a conceptual consciousness. The false step is the inference that comfort makes art a spare pleasure. Knowledge by abstractions remains, so the need to bring metaphysical abstractions into perceptual awareness remains. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Why does meeting practical needs not retire the need for art?

choices.text: The need follows from the kind of consciousness man has, not from an empty purse
Practical needs are unreal, so only art is a need
Art is a luxury, and luxuries become duties when one is rich
Comfort proves that abstractions are already perceptual

feedback.note: The need tracks conceptual consciousness, so a full purse does not end it. Practical needs are real; the error is not solved by calling them unreal. Wealth does not turn a luxury into this need, because art was not a luxury. Comfort does not make abstractions into percepts. The gap those abstractions leave is still there.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to the status this account gives it.

pairs.right: Not a reason for art to become optional
The status this account denies to art
The source of the need
What art is not, even in a comfortable life

feedback.note: Met practical needs do not retire art, luxury and spare pleasure are the status denied to it, and conceptual consciousness is why the need exists. A comfortable life can include art without turning art into an extra. The error is to think that once the body is provided for, the mind's kind of need has been answered. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Complete the denial of the claim that art is a luxury.

parts.text: added after practical needs are met.

feedback.note: Need is the status, and luxury is the status denied. Ornament and extra are the same mistake in other words: something added once practical life is secure. The sentence does not deny that food and shelter are needs. It denies that their satisfaction makes a concretized metaphysics optional for a conceptual mind.

exercises.prompt: Which remark states the luxury error in the language of a finished life?

choices.text: Art is an ornament for people who have already lived, not a requirement of conceptual life
Man needs art because his knowledge is conceptual
Food does not take the place of a concretized metaphysics
A need of man's kind of consciousness is not optional

feedback.note: An ornament for people who have already lived is the luxury claim: art comes after life and is not required by it. The other lines deny that claim. Conceptual knowledge is why the need exists, food does not replace it, and the need is not optional. The first remark treats a requirement of awareness as a trim on a life already complete.

exercises.prompt: Someone says art is a luxury because it does not bake bread. What confusion is that?

choices.text: It confuses a need of conceptual consciousness with a tool of physical production
It shows that only bread is real
It shows that art is identical with a loaf
It shows that production and consciousness are the same fact

feedback.note: Baking bread is a practical function. Art is a need because a conceptual mind must bring its widest abstractions into perceptual awareness. Failure to bake does not make that need a luxury. Bread is not the only reality, art is not a loaf, and production is not the same fact as consciousness. The confusion is the single standard of physical output.

exercises.prompt: Build the denial in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: Art is not a luxury added after practical needs are met. Calling it a spare pleasure one may skip is the claim being denied. The substitutes change the meaning into the error. Practical provision is real, and it does not close the need of a mind that knows by abstractions and must see its metaphysics in concrete form.

exercises.prompt: Which picture of the timing does this account reject?

choices.text: Thinking is finished first, and art is attached afterward as decoration
Art concretizes the metaphysical abstractions thinking has to grasp
A conceptual mind needs its abstractions in perceptual form
The need exists because man knows by abstractions

feedback.note: The rejected picture puts a finished thought first and art on afterward as decoration. Concretizing the abstractions, needing them in perceptual form, and tracing the need to conceptual knowledge are the account itself. Decoration attached later treats the need as an ornament on thinking that is already over.

exercises.prompt: What is wrong with calling art a decoration on a completed thought?

choices.text: It treats art as trim added when thinking is over, not as a need of the conceptual mind
It admits that thought uses concepts
It admits that a work of art can be perceived
It rightly makes the decoration do the work of knowing the facts

feedback.note: Trim added when thinking is over is the afterward picture. Thought does use concepts, and art can be perceived; those admissions are not the error. Making the decoration do the knowing would turn art into a tool of cognition, which is a further mistake. The error in the phrase is the timing: the need is not a frame nailed on after the thinking ends. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: A student finishes an argument that the universe is knowable, closes the notebook, and only then allows a novel as a reward. What has been separated?

choices.text: The thinking from the art, as if the need began only after thought was finished
Nothing, because a reward is how a conceptual mind holds an abstraction
The novel from perception, which improves the argument
Food from shelter, which retires every need of consciousness

feedback.note: The reward picture says thinking finishes and art may then be permitted. That separates the need from the conceptual mind and dates it after the work of thought. A reward is not how an abstraction is held in perceptual form. Cutting the novel off from perception would defeat concretization. Food and shelter do not retire the need either. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Match each picture of art to the verdict on its timing.

pairs.right: The timing this account rejects
The false picture of a mind that no longer needs art
Art belongs to the way that mind grasps its abstractions
What still has to be seen, not an ornament on a closed system

feedback.note: Later decoration and finished-first thinking are the rejected timing. The need belongs to the conceptual mind's grasp of its abstractions, and concretized metaphysics is what that mind still has to see. A closed notebook does not make the abstractions perceptually present. The ornament theory says the seeing is optional once the prose exists.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejected picture of when art arrives.

feedback.note: Decoration names the false status, and finished names the false timing. Proof would turn art into an argument, and optional would turn it into a luxury. The rejected picture is specifically afterward: thought ends, then trim is added. The need is to bring the abstractions into awareness, which a completed prose argument has not by itself done. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Which advice repeats the same timing in scholarly dress?

choices.text: First complete your philosophy, and only then, if effort remains, look at art
A philosophy of existence is among the abstractions art can concretize
The mind does not outgrow the need by reaching a conclusion
Showing a metaphysics is not the same as being finished with it

feedback.note: Complete the philosophy first, and look at art only if effort remains, is the afterward picture plus the luxury picture. The other lines keep art tied to the abstractions: it can concretize them, the need survives the conclusion, and showing is not the same as being done. Spare effort is not the condition of the need. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: A metaphysics is written out in prose. On this account, what is still missing for the conceptual mind?

choices.text: The abstractions in a form one can perceive, which finished prose does not supply
Nothing, because the prose has finished the thinking
A decoration that must not refer to the metaphysics
An escape from the metaphysics into a mood

feedback.note: Prose can state the metaphysics and still leave it short of immediate perceptual awareness. That awareness is what art supplies by concretizing it. Finished thinking does not close the need. Decoration that must not refer to the metaphysics, and a mood that escapes it, both refuse the concretization. The missing thing is the perceptible form of the very abstractions the prose stated.

exercises.prompt: Build the rejected timing in the order that keeps the error clear.

feedback.note: Art is not decoration attached after thinking is finished. A spare reward once philosophy is done is the same error in the language of a prize. The substitutes would affirm the timing this account rejects. The conceptual mind needs the abstractions in perceptual form as part of holding them, not as trim awarded after the holding is supposed to be over. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: Why does the need for art arise in a conceptual mind?

choices.text: Man must bring his widest metaphysical abstractions into immediate perceptual awareness
Man is bored once food and shelter are secure
Man needs a decoration once thinking is finished
Man needs feeling to discover the facts his concepts cannot reach

feedback.note: The need arises because conceptual knowledge is abstract, and the widest metaphysical abstractions have to become immediately perceptible. Boredom after comfort is the luxury error. Decoration after thought is the afterward error. Feeling as a discovery of facts treats emotion as a tool of cognition. None of those is the reason.

exercises.prompt: What does concretizing metaphysics supply to a conceptual mind?

choices.text: Immediate perceptual awareness of abstractions too wide for a single percept
A proof that replaces the need to think
A record of every fact, with nothing omitted
A fantasy cut off from existence

feedback.note: Concretization puts the metaphysical abstractions into a form one can perceive. It does not replace thinking with a proof, because art shows rather than teaches. An unselective record omits nothing and is not this concretization. A fantasy cut off from existence is not a re-creation of reality. The supply is perceptual awareness of a view, not a substitute for the view.

exercises.prompt: A person grasps in concepts that man can choose, but the idea stays pale until a play shows a choice and its outcome. What did the play supply?

choices.text: The abstraction in immediate perceptual form, which is the need art meets
A proof of volition that no reasoning could approach
A luxury, because the concept was already possessed
Decoration, because the thinking was finished before the curtain

feedback.note: The play makes the abstraction of volition perceptible in a choice and its outcome. It does not prove volition; the concept was already a conceptual grasp, and feeling or drama does not discover the fact. Possession of the concept does not make the showing a luxury, and a raised curtain is not decoration on finished thought. The paleness was the missing perceptual form.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the explanation to its role.

pairs.right: Too large to be held as a single percept
Metaphysics given a form one can perceive
What the conceptual mind needs those abstractions brought into
The rival that treats the need as a new tool of cognition

feedback.note: The abstractions are too wide for one percept, concretization gives metaphysics a perceptible form, and perceptual awareness is the state the mind needs. Feeling as a proof is the rival error. Art meets the need by showing, not by discovering facts the concepts failed to reach. The explanation is psycho-epistemological: how a conceptual mind holds its widest view. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Complete how art meets the need, and what it does not do.

feedback.note: Concretizing names the supply: a perceptible form of the metaphysical abstractions. Proving would make art a lecture or a tool of cognition, which the purpose rules out. Erasing would drop the metaphysics, and pricing would replace it with a cost. The need is awareness of a view one can grasp conceptually, not a new way to discover that the view is true. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Someone grants that art concretizes a metaphysics, then says the feeling of the work has thereby proved it. What is confused?

choices.text: Perceptual awareness of a view is treated as a proof of that view
The widest abstractions are treated as too large for one percept
Art is treated as showing a metaphysics rather than lecturing it
The need is tied to a mind that knows by abstractions

feedback.note: Concretizing makes a metaphysical view perceptible. It does not prove the view, because art shows and a feeling is not a tool of cognition. The other lines are parts of the account: the width of the abstractions, showing rather than teaching, and the conceptual mind. The confusion is taking the supply of awareness for evidence that the metaphysics is true.

exercises.prompt: Which account confuses this need with mysticism?

choices.text: Art opens a revelation beyond reason, so the abstractions need not be ones the mind can define
Art makes a reasoned view of existence perceptible
The abstractions belong to a conceptual consciousness
The need is to see what one can already hold in concepts

feedback.note: A revelation beyond reason, cut off from definable abstractions, is mysticism. The need is the opposite: a reasoned metaphysical view, held in concepts, brought into perceptual awareness. The other lines state that rational relation. Art does not bypass the conceptual mind. It gives that mind's widest abstractions a form the mind can perceive.

exercises.prompt: Build the reason for the need in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A conceptual mind needs its widest abstractions brought into immediate perceptual awareness. Stored as a luxury, or added after thinking is finished, are the two errors this reason rules out. The substitutes change the claim because the need follows from how man knows, not from spare time and not from a closed notebook.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states the full claim about why man needs art?

choices.text: Art is a need of a conceptual consciousness, not a luxury added after thought is finished
Art is a luxury of a conceptual consciousness, added after thought is finished
Art is a need of a mind that never forms concepts
Art is decoration attached once a philosophy has been proved

feedback.note: The full claim names the kind of mind and denies both the luxury status and the afterward timing. Reversing need into luxury, assigning the need to a nonconceptual mind, and calling art decoration on a proof each drop half of the claim. The reason is that wide abstractions must be brought into immediate perceptual awareness.

exercises.prompt: A reader calls art optional because she already accepts that the universe is knowable, and she has food. Which errors are combined?

choices.text: The luxury error and the afterward error: comfort and a finished idea are treated as retiring the need
A mere slip about the spelling of need
A correct statement that concepts are already perceptions
A correct statement that art has proved the metaphysics she accepts

feedback.note: Food is the luxury error, and a metaphysics she already accepts is the afterward error. Together they treat the need as retired. Spelling is not the issue. Concepts are not already perceptions, which is why the need arises. Art does not prove her metaphysics; it can concretize it. Both excuses leave the perceptual gap untouched.

exercises.prompt: What remains necessary after a metaphysics is stated in prose and practical life is secure?

choices.text: Bringing those abstractions into immediate perceptual awareness
Nothing esthetic, because both excuses have been satisfied
A propaganda poster that orders agreement with the prose
An unselective record of the day's events

feedback.note: Secure life and finished prose are the two excuses, and neither supplies perceptual awareness of the abstractions. A poster orders agreement instead of showing the view. An unselective record does not concretize a metaphysics. What remains necessary is the need itself: the widest abstractions in a form the conceptual mind can perceive at once.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the full claim to the point it secures.

pairs.right: The mind that has the need
Practical security does not retire art
Finished prose does not retire art
The reason the need remains in both cases

feedback.note: The mind is conceptual, luxury is denied because comfort does not retire the need, decoration afterward is denied because prose does not retire it, and perceptual awareness of the abstractions is why it remains. Dropping any part lets one of the excuses back in. The claim is one requirement, not a list of optional ornaments.

exercises.prompt: Complete the full claim in a single statement.

parts.text: Art is a need of a
consciousness, not a luxury added after thought is

feedback.note: Conceptual names the mind, and finished names the timing the luxury phrase pretends is enough. Perceptual would name a different kind of awareness, the one that does not have this need by itself. Optional would grant the luxury. The statement keeps both denials inside the positive claim about a conceptual consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Someone grants every clause except the width of the abstractions, and says art is needed only for small practical tips. What is cut out?

choices.text: The scale of the metaphysical abstractions the mind must make perceptible
The fact that man eats
The fact that a poster can be printed
The rule that art should teach a slogan

feedback.note: Small practical tips are not the widest metaphysical abstractions. Cutting the scale turns art into a handbook. Eating is a practical need and is not what was cut. Printing a poster is not the need. Teaching a slogan is the purpose art does not have. What was removed is the metaphysical width that makes perceptual concretization necessary.

exercises.prompt: Which whole verdict is consistent with the claim?

choices.text: Because man knows by abstractions, he needs art to see his metaphysics, and neither comfort nor a finished argument removes that need
Because man knows by abstractions, art is a spare pleasure he may skip
Because man knows by the immediate moment alone, art is his metaphysical need
Because feelings discover facts, art is the proof of his metaphysics

feedback.note: Knowledge by abstractions is why he needs to see his metaphysics in concrete form, and neither comfort nor a finished argument removes it. A spare pleasure contradicts the need. The immediate moment alone is the wrong kind of mind. Feelings do not discover facts, so art is not a proof. Only the first verdict holds the claim together. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Build the full claim in the order that keeps its meaning.

tokens.text: , not a luxury after thought is finished

feedback.note: Art is a need of a conceptual consciousness, not a luxury after thought is finished. A spare pleasure and decoration attached later are the two denials turned into affirmations. The substitutes change the claim. The reason they are false is the same: widest metaphysical abstractions still have to be brought into immediate perceptual awareness. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: What is a theme, as against a summary or a slogan?

choices.text: The work's abstract meaning
The list of events in their order
The skill with which the sentences are made
A slogan pasted beside the work

feedback.note: A theme is the work's abstract meaning. A list of events is a plot summary, skill is a verdict about execution, and a slogan beside the work is not the meaning the concretes carry. Those three are the usual substitutes. None of them is an abstract meaning embodied in the work. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Which question is the one that asks for the theme of a work?

choices.text: What abstract meaning do these chosen concretes carry?
What happens in one chapter, and then in the next?
What price did the manuscript bring?
Does the reader already agree with the author?

feedback.note: The theme question asks for the abstract meaning carried by the concretes the artist chose. Chapter order is a plot summary. A price is a market fact. Prior agreement is a philosophical question, not the meaning of this work. Asking those instead leaves the theme unnamed. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: A reader says, "The theme is bravery, because bravery is a trait I like." What is confused?

choices.text: The work's abstract meaning is replaced by the reader's preference
A theme is correctly identified as an abstract meaning
The concretes are correctly treated as the carriers
A plot summary is correctly kept out of the theme

feedback.note: Liking bravery substitutes the reader's preference for the meaning the work carries. That is subjectivism. A theme is an abstract meaning, the concretes are the carriers, and a plot summary is not the theme. The remark uses none of those disciplines. It names a favorite trait and calls the favorite the theme. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to what it is, or is not, in a work.

pairs.right: The work's abstract meaning
A retelling of the events
A sentence that is not the meaning inside the work
How well a meaning is embodied, not the meaning itself

feedback.note: The theme is the abstract meaning. A plot summary retells events, a slogan sits outside the work, and skill grades the embodiment. Confusing any of those with the theme names something that is not a meaning, or not this work's meaning. The carriers are the concretes, which none of the three substitutes are.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast between a theme and a summary.

feedback.note: Meaning names the theme, and summary names the retelling that is not a theme. Price is a market substitute, and mood is an emotion-oriented substitute. Neither is the work's abstract meaning. The sentence keeps the first distinction in place: what the work means, as against what happens in it. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: Which of these items is not a meaning of a work at all?

choices.text: The sale price of the canvas
That a human being can choose his course
That effort can succeed in the world
That a person bears the consequences of his choice

feedback.note: A sale price is not an abstract meaning of a work. The other three can be themes, because each is a meaning about man or existence that concretes could carry. They are not thereby the theme of every work. The price cannot be a theme of any work, because it does not appraise man or existence at all.

exercises.prompt: An author says the theme is loyalty, but nothing in the work concerns loyalty or any wider idea. What follows?

choices.text: A word the author likes is not the theme if it is not the work's meaning
The author's label is the theme by his stipulation
Any single noun is an abstract meaning of the work
A theme does not have to be in the work

feedback.note: The theme is the work's meaning, not a word the author enjoys. Stipulation, the magic of a noun, and a theme that need not be in the work all detach the meaning from the concretes. If loyalty is not what the work presents, loyalty is not its theme. The label does not create the meaning it names.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition of a theme in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A theme is the work's abstract meaning. A plot summary and a pasted slogan are the two substitutes. Either one changes the definition, because a retelling of events is not a meaning, and a sentence beside the work is not the meaning the work carries. The theme is what the chosen concretes mean.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between a theme and a plot summary?

choices.text: A theme is the abstract meaning; a plot summary retells the events
They are two names for the same chapter list
A plot summary is the meaning, and the theme is the list of events
A theme is the climax, counted as one event

feedback.note: The theme is abstract meaning, and the summary retells events. They are not two names for a chapter list, and reversing them swaps meaning with narrative. The climax is one event in a purposeful progression, not the theme. A summary can be accurate and still not say what the events mean. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: "She refuses the bribe, loses the post, and keeps the friend who told the truth." Why is that not yet the theme?

choices.text: It retells events, and the theme would be the abstract meaning those events carry
It is already the theme, because events are abstractions
It is the theme because it is shorter than the novel
It is the theme because a friend is mentioned

feedback.note: Refusing, losing, and keeping are events. The theme would be the meaning they carry, such as the place of honesty in a life one can respect. Events are not already abstractions of that kind. Shorter length and the presence of a friend do not produce a meaning. The sentence is a plot summary. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a theme rather than a summary?

choices.text: A person can refuse an unearned gain and still face his own life
Mara refuses the bribe in chapter twelve and walks home
The book has forty chapters and a coastal setting
The actress who played Mara later gave an interview

feedback.note: The first sentence states an abstract meaning about a person and a value. Chapter twelve and the walk home are events. Chapter count and setting are surface facts. An interview is outside the work. Only the first can be a theme, and it is a theme of a work only if that work's concretes carry it. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to the kind of report it is.

pairs.left: She leaves, returns, and confronts her partner
pairs.right: A plot summary

pairs.left: Independence is a condition of self-respect
pairs.right: A theme, if the concretes carry it

pairs.left: The confrontation that resolves the choice
pairs.right: A climax, which is one event in the plot

pairs.left: The city where the events are placed
pairs.right: A setting, not a meaning

feedback.note: The summary retells events, the theme states a meaning, the climax is a resolving event, and the city is a setting. A plot, understood as a purposeful progression toward a climax, is still not the theme. Naming the progression accurately does not yet name what it means. Setting and climax are concretes, not the abstraction.

exercises.prompt: Complete the division between retelling and meaning.

feedback.note: Events are what a summary retells, and meaning is what a theme names. Chapters are a count of divisions, and prices are a market fact. Neither is the abstract content. The division matters because a purposeful plot can be summarized without anyone having stated the view of man and existence the plot carries.

exercises.prompt: A plot is a purposeful progression toward a climax. Why is naming that progression still not naming the theme?

choices.text: The progression is the concrete action; the theme is the abstract meaning it carries
A plot and a theme are identical by definition
A climax is the theme because it comes last
Purpose erases meaning, so a plotted work has no theme

feedback.note: The progression is what happens, purposefully and in logical connection. The theme is what that action means. They are not identical. Coming last does not turn a climax into an abstraction. Purpose does not erase meaning; it is often what carries the meaning. Stating the plot's shape still leaves the theme to be named.

exercises.prompt: Which mistake treats a surface detail as the theme?

choices.text: The theme is the red coat, because the coat appears in three scenes
The coat is a concrete that may help carry a meaning
Repeating a detail is not itself an abstract meaning
A meaning has to be wider than one prop

feedback.note: Repetition does not turn a coat into a meaning. The coat can be a concrete that carries a theme, which is a different claim. The error is identifying the prop with the abstraction. A theme has to be wider than the prop, precisely because it is the meaning the prop helps carry, not the prop itself.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A theme is not a retelling of the events. A list of chapters in the order they occur is that retelling under another description. The substitutes would turn the sentence into a summary of the summary. The theme remains the abstract meaning, which a complete and orderly account of the events can still fail to state. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: What are the concretes that carry a theme?

choices.text: The particulars the artist chose to include, omit, or stress
Every particular that existed near the artist, chosen or not
The abstract meaning, under another name
A slogan the publisher attaches later

feedback.note: The concretes are the particulars the artist chose: what is included, omitted, and stressed. The unselected remainder was not put into the work. The abstract meaning is the theme, not the concrete. A later slogan is outside the choice. Carrying is done by the selected particulars, not by whatever happened to be nearby. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: What do the concretes the artist chose do for the theme?

choices.text: They carry the theme
They replace the theme with a plot summary
They remain decorative and carry nothing
They prove the theme the way evidence proves a theory

feedback.note: The concretes carry the abstract meaning; that is their role. They are not a plot summary, and they are not decoration attached after the meaning is finished. They also do not prove the theme. Art shows the meaning; it does not discover it as a tool of cognition. Carrying is embodiment, not demonstration.

exercises.prompt: A painter includes a standing figure, omits the crowd, and stresses the light on the face, to present man as able to face existence. Which items are the concretes?

choices.text: The figure, the omitted crowd, and the stressed light
The sentence on the wall label
The viewer's agreement with that sentence
The price of the frame

feedback.note: The figure, the omission, and the stress are the particulars the painter chose, and they are what can carry the meaning. The wall label is a slogan beside the work. Agreement is a viewer's philosophical response. The frame's price is not a concrete of the picture. Only the selected particulars do the carrying. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: Match each concrete to the job it can do for a theme.

pairs.right: Kept because the judgment treats it as essential
Left out so it will not carry the theme
Given weight so it carries more of the meaning
The theme those particulars carry

feedback.note: Inclusion, omission, and stress are the selection that decides which particulars carry the theme, and the abstract meaning is what they carry. Omission is part of the carrying, because what is left out is kept from competing with the meaning. The theme is not itself a concrete, and a concrete is not the theme.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about what carries the theme.

parts.text: The theme is carried by the

feedback.note: Concretes names the particulars, and chose names the selection. Slogans are sentences beside the work, and guessed would replace the judgment with a stab. The theme is not carried by the unselected remainder or by a label. It is carried by what the artist included, omitted, and stressed. That reading fails because it answers a different question.

exercises.prompt: Why is "the theme is carried by whatever happened to be in the street" wrong?

choices.text: The carriers are the particulars the artist chose, not the unselected remainder
A street cannot appear in a work of art
Choice would make the work deterministic
Omission always turns the work into a fantasy

feedback.note: The street's remainder was not chosen, so it is not in the work as a carrier. A street can appear if the artist selects it. Choice is selection, not determinism. Omission is part of selection and does not by itself cut the work off from reality. The error treats an unselective record as if it carried a theme.

exercises.prompt: A novelist is tempted to add a subplot that does not bear on the meaning. What would adding it for its own sake do?

choices.text: It would put in a concrete that does not carry the theme
It would automatically widen the abstract meaning
It would turn the subplot into a proof of the theme
It would make selection unnecessary

feedback.note: A subplot that does not bear on the meaning is a particular that fails to carry the theme. It does not widen the meaning merely by being added, and it does not prove anything. Selection remains necessary; the temptation is a proposal to ignore it. The concretes that carry are the ones chosen because of the meaning, not the ones collected beside it.

exercises.prompt: Build the carrying claim in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: The concretes the artist chose carry the theme. A pasted slogan and the unselected remainder do not. The substitutes change the claim, because carrying is done by the particulars that were included, omitted, and stressed according to the meaning. What was never chosen, and what was pasted beside the work, is not that carrier.

exercises.prompt: How is a theme present in a work, as against a label beside it?

choices.text: It is carried by the concretes, not supplied by a slogan attached beside them
It is the card beside the work, whatever the concretes do
It is a plot summary read aloud at the door
It is the viewer's vote

feedback.note: The theme is carried by the concretes the artist chose. A card beside the work, a summary read at the door, and a viewer's vote are all outside that carrying. The vote is subjectivism. The card can contradict the picture and still not win, because a slogan does not supply the meaning the concretes fail to carry.

exercises.prompt: The painting shows a man turning from a bribe. The catalog says the theme is despair. The picture does not show despair. Which is the work's theme?

choices.text: The meaning the pictured choice carries, not the catalog's word
Despair, because the catalog is attached
Both, because a slogan and a contradictory picture share one theme
Neither, because a theme must be a plot summary

feedback.note: The pictured refusal carries whatever meaning that choice embodies, and the catalog's despair does not override it. Attachment does not make a word the theme. A contradictory slogan and picture do not share a theme; the work's theme is the one in the concretes. A plot summary is not required, and it would not be the theme either.

exercises.prompt: A true slogan is pasted beside a muddled work. What can be true, and what is still not the theme?

choices.text: The slogan may be true as philosophy, and it is still not the work's theme
Truth makes the slogan the theme of the muddled work
The muddle makes the true slogan false
A theme is whatever is true, whether or not this work carries it

feedback.note: Philosophical truth and esthetic carrying come apart. The slogan can be true and still not be this work's theme, because the concretes do not carry it. Truth does not migrate into the muddle. The muddle does not falsify the sentence. And a theme is this work's meaning, not every truth that exists outside it.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the status it has for the theme.

pairs.right: The theme is in the particulars the artist chose
A sentence beside the work, not the meaning inside it
A philosophical claim this work has not carried
A word that cannot overrule the concretes

feedback.note: Embodiment puts the theme in the chosen particulars. A pasted slogan, a true sentence the work does not show, and a label that contradicts the picture are all outside that carrying. None of them overrules the concretes. The theme is identified by what is shown, not by what is printed beside the showing.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast between carrying and attaching.

feedback.note: Carried names embodiment, and pasted names the slogan attached beside the work. Proved would turn the concretes into a demonstration, which is not what art does. Priced would turn the theme into a cost. The meaning is in the particulars the artist chose. A true card on the wall does not become that meaning.

exercises.prompt: Which practice turns the work into a propaganda poster?

choices.text: Letting the slogan do the work, while the concretes are only an excuse for the order
Selecting concretes that show a view of man
Omitting particulars that do not carry the meaning
Stressing the act that embodies the theme

feedback.note: When the slogan gives an order and the concretes are only an excuse, the work teaches a command instead of showing a meaning. That is a propaganda poster. Selecting, omitting, and stressing so that the concretes carry a view of man are the method of a theme. They are not propaganda. The failure is the substitution of the order for the carrying. The rival fails because it changes the principle.

exercises.prompt: The concretes carry the view that man is determined, and the wall text says man is free. You hold that man is free. What is the work's theme?

choices.text: That man is determined, because that is the meaning the concretes carry
That man is free, because the wall text says so
That man is free, because you welcome that conclusion
There is no theme, because you oppose determinism

feedback.note: The theme is the meaning the concretes carry, here the deterministic view, even though you reject it and even though the wall text disagrees. Welcoming freedom does not rewrite the work, and opposition does not erase the theme. The same standard identifies the theme of a work you oppose and of a work you welcome. Truth is a further question.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast in the order that keeps its meaning.

tokens.text: , not pasted on as a slogan

feedback.note: A theme is carried by the concretes, not pasted on as a slogan. The wall text and a command are the pasted substitutes, including the propaganda form. They change the claim because they locate the meaning outside the particulars the artist chose. A contradictory label cannot overrule what those particulars show.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence states the full claim about a theme?

choices.text: A theme is the work's abstract meaning, carried by the concretes the artist chose
A theme is a plot summary, pasted beside the work as a slogan
A theme is the artist's mood, discovered by feeling as a fact
A theme is the reader's agreement, which creates the meaning

feedback.note: The full claim joins the abstract meaning to the concretes that carry it. A plot summary pasted as a slogan combines the two substitutes. A mood discovered as a fact treats feeling as a tool of cognition. The reader's agreement creates nothing in the work; that is subjectivism. Only the first sentence keeps meaning and carrier together.

exercises.prompt: A scientist checks his figures, rejects a flattering error, and publishes the correction at a cost. No preface states a thesis. The selection stresses that sequence. What is the theme?

choices.text: A mind can choose truth over a flattering falsehood, which is the meaning those concretes carry
That a scientist publishes, which is the plot summary
Nothing, because the preface is blank
The cost, because a cost is a concrete and a concrete is a theme

feedback.note: The stressed sequence carries an abstract meaning about choosing truth over a flattering falsehood. Publishing is the summary of an event. A blank preface does not erase a meaning the concretes carry. The cost is one concrete, not the theme. The theme is the meaning, and it does not need a slogan in order to be present.

exercises.prompt: The same events are summarized as "he checks, he rejects, he publishes," and a poster adds "Obey the academy." Why do both miss the theme?

choices.text: The summary retells events, and the poster pastes a slogan the concretes do not carry
Both are themes, because a summary and a slogan are meanings
The poster is the theme, because an order outranks a story
The summary is the theme, because it is complete

feedback.note: The summary is not the abstract meaning, and the order to obey is not what the correction carries. If anything, the concretes carry a refusal to accept a flattering falsehood, which conflicts with obedience as the point. An order does not outrank the story. Completeness of a retelling does not turn it into a theme. Both miss what the chosen events mean.

exercises.prompt: Match each name to the place it has in the full claim.

pairs.right: What a theme is
What carries that meaning
A retelling that is not the theme
A sentence beside the work that is not the theme

feedback.note: The claim needs the meaning and the carrier, and it excludes the summary and the slogan. A retelling can be accurate, and a slogan can be true, without either being the theme. The theme is present when the particulars the artist chose embody the abstraction. It is not present when only the card or the chapter list is doing the talking. The substitute fails because it drops the distinction.

exercises.prompt: Complete the full claim about what a theme is and what carries it.

parts.text: A theme is the work's abstract

feedback.note: Meaning names what the theme is, and concretes names what carries it. Summary is the plot retelling, and slogan is the pasted sentence. Either substitute breaks the claim. The artist chose those concretes by including, omitting, and stressing. What they carry is the theme, whether or not a preface agrees. The alternative fails because it does not state this claim.

exercises.prompt: A deterministic plot is skillfully carried, and you reject determinism. What do you call the theme, and what do you not conclude?

choices.text: The theme is the deterministic meaning the concretes carry, and that does not make the philosophy true
The theme is your own philosophy, because you oppose the book
There is no theme, because a false meaning cannot be carried
The theme is the skill itself

feedback.note: The theme is the abstract meaning the concretes carry, which is deterministic, and skill does not make that philosophy true. Your opposition does not install your own view as the theme. A false meaning can be carried; that is one direction in which skill and truth come apart. Skill is not the meaning. The same standard names the theme you reject.

exercises.prompt: Which work has a theme on the full claim?

choices.text: The particulars were chosen so their meaning is that man can choose, and no external slogan is required
The events are listed, and the meaning is whatever a crowd feels
A true sentence is framed beside an unrelated pattern
Every street fact is recorded at equal weight, and no meaning is stressed

feedback.note: Chosen particulars that mean man can choose, without a slogan, meet the claim. A crowd's feeling is subjectivism and does not read the concretes. A true sentence beside an unrelated pattern is pasted, not carried. An equal record of street facts is an unselective record and stresses no meaning. Only the first work has a theme in the required sense.

exercises.prompt: Build the full claim in the order that keeps its meaning.

feedback.note: A theme is the work's abstract meaning carried by the concretes the artist chose. A plot summary and a slogan pasted beside it are the substitutes the claim excludes. Either one changes the sentence, because retelling events is not the meaning, and a sentence outside the work is not what the chosen particulars show.
